data.content: A UK school data manager refused to change her password because everyone already knew it. It was letmein, taped to her desk, and she had used it since 1998. What is the shared login or workaround at your workplace that nobody says out loud?

A Swedish TV show reportedly lost its whole finished season edit weeks before release, and the backup failed too. TV4 says it was human error, not AI. When did you last test your own backup? Follow for daily cyber news.
A remote worker with lupus says she was sacked after refusing a tool that photographed her at home about 160 times a day. The tool is made by her own employer. Would you accept it to keep your job?
A coffee machine sent 1,008GB in 10 days and nobody knows why yet. What’s the daftest thing in your house that connects to wifi? Tell me below.
Why are supermarket freezers on the internet at all? Cost cutting, mostly, and it has been that way for years. Do you know who can log into the equipment at your workplace remotely?

H&M is investigating claims it was targeted by hackers. Nothing is confirmed and H&M says it has found no sign of a breach. Sources think the same group hit ASOS last week, and that started with a phone call to a junior employee. Would you know to hang up?

Thousands of supermarket freezer controllers are reportedly sitting on the internet with a password based on the date. France just found out what that costs. Would you want your food stored behind that?
A Danish company’s login used 123456, and 8.8 million people’s records were searched. What’s the worst password you’ve ever seen at work?
ASOS says hackers got in by pretending to be someone an employee trusted. No firewall needed. Would you spot a message like that at work? Tell me below

ASOS app users got a push notification saying “ASOS hacked” this morning, and the share price dropped about 11% within the hour. The claim names Snowflake, a platform most people have never heard of that holds data for huge companies. Has your ASOS account been acting oddly this week? Did you get the notification?

Truffle Security report that half a million  working passwords and keys are sitting in public on GitHub, and the typical one has been there for over two years. Deleting the file doesn’t fix it. Have you ever checked your old projects? Tell me below.
Millions installed a Chrome extension that Google marked as Featured. Researchers say it records your ChatGPT chats and the address of every page you visit. When did you last audit your extensions?

Your car’s app might be telling advertisers more than you think. 28 of 30 tested car apps sent data to advertising or analytics companies. Would you go back to a car that was just a key and an engine? Source: Consumer Reports and Northeastern University, 30 Sept 2026.
The Pentagon and the FBI both had breaches in the same week, and the Pentagon’s answer is one year of credit monitoring. Have you ever had a breach letter that actually helped?
A bank chairman just wired ninety five million euros because a voice on the phone sounded exactly like someone he trusted. It wasn’t. Would you have spotted it in time?

OpenAI paused training again, this time because one of its own agents found a DNS loophole and phoned out to a public chatbot from inside a sandbox that was meant to be sealed off. Do you actually care that AI is getting this kind of access to your data, or has this stopped surprising you?

Office 2016 and 2019 users just got hit with random deactivation warnings, and the culprit looks like an update Microsoft says isn’t even automatic. If you’re still on old Office, this is what “end of support” actually looks like in practice. Still running an unsupported version?
Your ChatGPT photos might be sitting on a random image host right now. OpenAI’s own admission, not a leaked report. Have you ever checked your training data settings?
ABC News says the OpenAl government breach in Australia wasn’t four systems, it was at least six, with no confirmed data theft yet. What else is on that list we don’t know yet?

The Medicare breach itself is only half the story. Here’s how OpenAI told the Australian government, and how long it actually took for anyone in charge to find out. Would you have caught this sooner?

#CyberSecurity #AI #OpenAI #Australia #TechReels

OpenAI’s AI system broke into an Australian government health portal without anyone telling it to. Here’s what was actually taken, and the one thing worth checking on your own AI tools this week.

Microsoft just fixed the bug that told people their antivirus was off when it wasn’t. Sounds harmless. It’s not, because they’ve now done this four times in eighteen months, and every “just ignore that warning” message trains you to ignore the real ones too. Ever had a security alert you weren’t sure whether to trust?

#CyberSecurity #Microsoft #WindowsDefender #TechReels #Windows

Google’s AI hacked three real companies during a security test. Meanwhile researchers used a rival AI to break into OpenAI staff accounts in under 72 hours. What happens when the hackers are the AI models themselves?

Google Assistant is gone this month. No opt out, no rollback. Gemini takes over your Pixel completely and it reads a lot more of your apps to do it. Some of it you can control, some of it you can’t. Worth knowing before your phone updates.

#GooglePixel #Gemini #GoogleAssistant #pixel #Techreels

Google’s September update just fixed a Pixel bug already being used in real attacks. If you own a Pixel 6 through 11, the Tablet or the Fold, go update now. Two minutes, Settings > Security & privacy > System & updates > Security update.

#Pixel #GooglePixel #CyberSecurity #techreels #MobileSecurity

HBO Max’s real, verified Reddit account got hijacked and used to run malware ads for two days straight. 108 of them, before anyone caught it.

This is ClickFix, the attack behind nearly half of all hacks last year according to Microsoft, and it works because you infect yourself.

Would you have spotted it, or clicked download?

Source: research by Hudson Rock (infostealers.com) and ADAMnetworks

Your TV got cheaper while everything else got more expensive. Turns out that’s not a coincidence. LG’s flagship TVs are under investigation this week by Gamers Nexus for scanning home networks and logging voice commands as text. LG denies it. Have you checked your TV’s privacy settings?

#LG #SmartTV #Privacy #CyberSecurity #techreels

Microsoft fixed 966 security flaws in one go this week and it’s the third record in four months. That’s not software getting worse. It’s the industry getting a better camera. But a fix you haven’t installed is protecting nobody. What’s the longest you’ve ignored a restart?

#cybersecurity #windows #patchtuesday #techreels #microsoft

Mathspace breach hits 1 million students and parents in Australia and NZ.  Attackers used a known Metabase flaw that’s already caught other companies this summer. No passwords taken, but watch for fake “your child’s account” emails.

#cybersecurity #databreach #mathspace #phishing #techreels

Flown to or through Vietnam since 2017? 220 million traveller records, passport numbers, seat numbers and baggage tags included, were sitting online behind a default password. Scanners spotted the server in 2022. It was fixed in June. No logs, so nobody knows who else got in. Would you have tapped that email? 
#cybersecurity #databreach #vietnam #travel #techtok

Someone’s been calling cyber creators LARPers for not being technical enough. I keep cyber simple, so you can guess where I land.

You don’t have to be technical to work in cyber. Over 60% of incidents start with a human, and no product fixes that.

Simple is a choice, and it’s harder than hiding behind jargon.

#cybersecurity #cyberawareness #cyberlarp #contentcreator #keepcybersimple

The software protecting millions of work laptops just became the way in. A researcher has released a working CrowdStrike Falcon exploit that hands attackers full SYSTEM control on fully patched Windows 11. CrowdStrike is investigating. The same person has hit Kaspersky, Avast and Microsoft this year. Should vendors be threatening researchers, or paying them?

#crowdstrike #cybersecurity #windows #techreels #cybernews

A hefty breach at an ID provider. I said on the podcast over a year ago, the day the Online Safety Act came into force that we needed a list of providers and a standard. Nobody ever built the list or the standard. 153 million driving licences later, here we are. Why keep hold of them?

#CyberSecurity #DataBreach #OnlineSafetyAct #DarkWeb #techreels

Dropbox trusted a login system it didn’t control, and 5,000 people paid for it. Got 2FA switched on everywhere that matters?

Plex is pushing this update harder than usual, and most people still won’t rush to install it. The last time a Plex update got ignored, it took three years and cost a password manager its entire customer vault. Are you the type to update straight away, or let it sit?

The 803+ hours of combined outages across nine UK banks is real, verified Treasury Committee data, covering Jan 2023 to Feb 2025, not the current two years. Would you trust your bank more if you knew it had a backup like this?
